fields.q: Refer to the value-of-money graph. The economy moves from a to b. Velocity is allowed to change. In a long-run comparison, a nominal wage rises by the same proportion as the price level inferred from those points, and technology and labor supplies are unchanged. Which comparison fits monetary neutrality?
fields.feedback: The graph gives value of money 2 at a and 1.5 at b. Their reciprocal price levels are 1/2 and 2/3, a one-third increase. Proportional nominal wage growth leaves the real wage unchanged; nominal changes alone do not raise real productive capacity. With real output fixed, this graph requires velocity to fall to two-thirds of its initial value; it is not the fixed-velocity quantity-theory case.
